text:
aya: Heads up — since the kernel-selector flip yesterday we're seeing a slow steady GPU memory growth on the 4xA100 test fleet. Not a hard OOM but nodes creep up ~10-15 MB/min until reclaim kicks in. Could be workspace sizing or a buffer that isn't reused across kernel variants.

sam: repro? steps + env?

aya: repro is flaky but here's the sequence that triggers 90%: run loadgen with batch_window=30ms, seq distribution heavy tail (512+), kernel-selector picks fused-attn-v2 for long seqs, then some requests hit legacy fused-attn path and allocate a second workspace. After a kernel flip under load the second workspace sticks around.

mike_p: can you paste the minimal repro? I can run on staging.

aya: gist-ish:
```
# simplified repro
RUNTIME_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=30 RUNTIME_KERNEL_POLICY=adaptive \
  ./loadgen --model llama-7b --seq-dist heavy_tail --qps 150 --duration 10m
```
observed: after ~4m resident set increases, nvtop shows additional large buffer per process.

katie_s: I grabbed a few profiler snapshots (nvprof + runtime heap dump). From heap: slab0: 512MB resident, slab1: 128MB resident, but slab1 holds many "workspace_temp" allocations with alloc_sites pointing to fused_attn_v2::alloc_workspace and fused_attn_v1::alloc_workspace. They don't get freed when kernel flips.

jordan: might be KV cache churn too — we changed batching heuristic to batch by arrival-time which increased prefix cache churn; that could inflate KV and by coincidence align with kernel-selector change. Do we have correlation per-request?

aya: I checked traces: KV size stable; the extra resident blocks are pure workspace buffers (large contiguous allocations). Stack traces show different kernel codepaths allocating similar sized buffers but with different pool keys, so reuse misses.

mike_p: quick hypothesis: workspace pool key includes kernel version string. When selector flips between v1/v2 we don't canonicalize key, so we end up with two separate entries and neither gets downsized. Fix: normalize workspace key to canonical sig (shape+type) rather than kernel id.

sam: ack. I can run a branch that canonicalizes pool keys. Also will try tuning allocator aging: RUNTIME_ALLOC_SLAB_MAX_AGE=30s to force earlier compaction.

aya: patch idea looks good. Also propose reusing buffers across kernel variants when shape/element-size match. That avoids double allocation and reduces fragmentation.

katie_s: perf CI snapshot after canonicalization + reuse shows promising numbers: before patch growth ~12 MB/min, after ~1.2 MB/min under same load. Peak resident down ~480MB -> ~80MB lower. NVPROF diff attached to CI (link: https://perf-ci/reports/1942/compare).

perf-ci: build 1942 completed — perf regression test: PASS (growth rate 1.2 MB/min, mem leak threshold 5 MB/min).

infra-bot: deploy staged/runtime@canary started by sam — rollout 10% -> 100% over 20m window.

mike_p: can we also add a unit test that simulates kernel flip and asserts workspace pool size stays bounded? small fuzz harness should do it.

aya: yes please. test should run in CI with mocked kernel ids. I'll write the test and the doc note. After test+patch we should backport to 2024.11 and schedule for Dedicated clusters.

sam: running staged job now on a3a-run4 (id: run-1942). Will report back in ~30m.

aya: thanks all. If staged looks good I'll open a PR for backport and include the perf snapshot.

jordan: quick note: follow-up work — consider making workspace pool policy aware of sequence-length distributions so we don't pre-allocate huge windows for short sequences (helps cost too).

aya: agreed. filing a ticket after this. :thumbsup:
